children: Morgans downgrades Qantas Airways to hold, from accumulate, as fuel costs creep higher against a backdrop of ongoing Middle East tensions. Qantas's 1H fuel bill is set to swell to A$3.75 billion. Still, Qantas says travel demand remains resilient. Analyst Chris Creech is positive on the quality of Qantas's business, pointing to its fleet-renewal program that should help to drive earnings growth over time. "However, elevated fuel prices, higher operating costs and broader inflationary pressures continue to weigh on near-term earnings, with FY27 underlying pretax profit expected to decline materially (-21%) on prior forecasts before earnings growth resumes from FY28 onwards," Morgans says. It views FY27 as a transition year for Qantas, which ended last week at A$9.45. (david.winning@wsj.com; @dwinningWSJ)
